items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: We had a good band down there. Dan Jackson.

ctx.x: Then they tore it down about four or five years ago. They tore it down? A big housing project. Yeah.

So we played down there after we leave the Dreamland. We'd go down to Pekin and stay there until four or five o'clock in the morning. We had a good band down there. Dan Jackson. I had that job. Dan Jackson was running old Mott Brunelaw. It was his father-in-law, brother. Man Jackson married his daughter. Our son's for Charlie McCurdies. He played in the theater and I had him to play, I believe, the theater down there too. He and Theo together on the clarinet. Charlie disappeared. Nobody ain't never know the day…
